Session context dump for T643 (per-harness progress watchdog). Raw evidence behind findings/T643-progress-fuse.json.

## (1) The defect, with the three kills
T214's progress watchdog fires at a flat --progress-timeout (600 s) with no [progress] line. T634 fixed the identical defect in the STARTUP fuse for claude (stdout is wrong for a buffering harness; mtime is right); the PROGRESS fuse kept the flat 600 s and today it killed three deepseek lanes doing normal long work. All three walls are BELOW the deepseek family p95:

| lane | model | wall at kill | artifact at kill | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T526 | deepseek-v4-flash | 1129.6 s | 870 uncommitted lines, no findings | untracked/log/t526.log: '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s (10'00) — no [progress] for 600s' / 'exit 124 ... in 1129.6 s' |
| T635 | deepseek-v4-pro | 1732.6 s | none | untracked/log/t635.log: '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s (10'00) — no [progress] for 600s' / 'exit 124 ... in 1732.6 s'; heartbeat line 6521 wall=1732.6 cpu=1566.6 |
| T638 | deepseek-v4-flash | 1901.3 s | complete — 25/25 verdicts | untracked/log/t638.log: 'KILL: progress timeout 600s' / 'exit 124 ... in 1901.3 s'; run record killed='progress timeout 600s' signal 9 wall 1901.3 |

T638 was killed having FINISHED (25/25 verdicts in findings/T638-race-g.json), exactly as T616 was under the startup fuse. T634's own measurement condemns the threshold: deepseek p95 wall was 2340.9 s (n=113); a 600 s fuse sits at roughly a quarter of that, so it catches normal long work, not stalls.

## (2) The sensor chosen, and why (mirrors T634)
For pi/ollama lanes the progress sensor is the existing stdout/stderr/[progress] signal PLUS the declared deliverables' mtime (the bundle's deliverables= header, resolved against repo_root). A working deepseek lane writes its deliverable while its stream is quiet (long reasoning stretches), so the deliverable mtime is the honest 'is it working' signal; a genuinely hung lane stops moving everything. The shared repo tree is deliberately NOT a sensor (other consoles write the same checkout — T634's exact reasoning). The scan is throttled to ~1 s and uses the same watermark pattern as T634's claude fuse.

## (3) Threshold derivation (derived, not chosen)
Computed from untracked/runs/*.json, snapshot 2026-08-22. Population: finalized runs carrying a wall reading, EXCLUDING (a) guard-killed runs (killed/signal present — truncated, would drag the p95 down in the dangerous direction) and (b) the T542 bakeoff gate sub-runs (bakeoff_* prefix, wall 0.0-0.6 s — a different harness shape, not worker lanes). Classified by child binary basename; p95 by linear interpolation; threshold = ceil(3 x p95):

| family (binary) | n | p95 (s) | 3 x p95 | default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pi (deepseek) | 66 | 2445.05 | 7335.15 | 7336 |
| ollama | 9 | 2255.02 | 6765.06 | 6766 |
| claude | 30 | 1534.91 | 4604.73 | (T634's 4631 stands; out of scope) |

Disagreement with T634, stated: T634 reported deepseek p95 2340.9 s (n=113). My snapshot is 2445.05 s (n=66). The denominators differ because (a) T634's n=113 included the 55 T542 bakeoff gate sub-runs (wall <= 0.6 s) which drag the p95 down, and (b) ~10 more deepseek runs landed since T634's 16:19Z snapshot, while the archive-2026-08-20 sweep moved 30 records out. Excluding bakeoff sub-runs is the conservative direction and required by '>= 3x p95'. Sanity check on methodology: the same filter on the claude family gives p95 1540.2 s (n=28, completed-only variant) — within 3 s of T634's 1543.5 s (n=29), so the filter reproduces T634's claude figure.

## (4) Kills are unscoreable
_killed_by maps any reason containing 'progress timeout' to 'watchdog' (T629's enumerated vocabulary). The new kill reason keeps the 'progress timeout' prefix, so a pi/ollama watchdog kill is stamped killed_by=watchdog on the run record and every scorer refuses it (Ruling 32: present, labeled censored, never scored). No second enum invented.

## (6) Margins under the new threshold
The threshold moved 600 s -> 7336 s (pi). Each real kill therefore survives by 7336 - 600 = 6736 s of additional quiet time before the watchdog could fire: T526 (1129.6 s wall) +6736 s, T635 (1732.6 s) +6736 s, T638 (1901.3 s) +6736 s. Additionally, the new deliverable-mtime sensor keeps a lane alive CONTINUOUSLY while it writes its declared deliverable: T638 (findings/T638-race-g.json, 25/25) and T526 (tools/bakeoff.sh + regression + findings, 870 uncommitted lines) would never even approach the threshold; T635 (no artifact) is protected by the larger threshold alone.
